- Info moves down from Application layer to physical layer
- Each layer adds its own header

SIGNAL TYPE Voltage(electrical current) Electromagnetic waves
- Bandwidth: Maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a network in a specific amount of time
- Throughput: Actual succesful data being transmitted
- Signal-to-noise ratio: Level of signal with the amount of noise. High signal means less packet loss, corrupt data.
- Latency: Amount of time it takes for a signal to travel from source to its destination and back.
- Jitter: Variation in latency over time, high jitter means packets arriving at inconsistent intervals instead of steadily.
- HUBS: Device with multiple ports, recieves a data frame at one port and broadcasts that to all other ports on the hub.
- REPEATERS: Signal booster, used to mitigate signal attenuation.
- CONCENTRATORS: Combine all signals for transmission down a single line.
